notes: No custom pleading is drafted on any CT composed route in this job. Every unit that would produce a court document is blocked on an unapproved filing vehicle or an unidentified official form, and each blocker is recorded in a dependency manifest naming the exact missing source.

ct-missed-erasure produces no court document at all: there is no court venue on that track — the destination is DESPP. No agency_request_letter is drafted either, because the § 54-142t(g) submission vehicle is precisely what is missing, and a letter would be the same invention under another name.

Two units are synthesized beyond the registry's own units[]: ct-missed-erasure unit 1 (the DPS-0846-C record request, recorded in the registry as a participantFilingRequirement) and ct-nolle-auto unit 3 (the pre-1 April 1972 petition, recorded only as a packetInstruction). Both are marked componentIdSynthesized and are justified in each route's omissionProof.

The JD-CR-202 conflict is the single highest-value item for review across this jurisdiction: the compiled profile treats JD-CR-202 as the vehicle for pre-2000 conviction petitions, the pinned registry says it is a Clean Slate form and not a § 54-142a(f)(2) form. The registry reading governs here and the conflict is recorded rather than resolved.
The compiled profile's 'SPBI check dated on/after 1/1/2024' rule conflicts with the registry, which records that reading as a probable misreading. No report-date rule is stated to any participant.
No fee figure is quoted to a participant anywhere in this job except the § 54-142a(k) no-fee rule, which is squarely sourced for § 54-142a filings and is never carried across to § 54-142d.
